Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors: 5

An ophthalmology patient receives a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor to reduce aqueous humor production. The same enzyme family also participates in renal bicarbonate handling. Which pharmacologic mechanism links the ocular and renal effects described?

  1. Carbonic anhydrase inhibition
  2. NKCC2 inhibition in the thick ascending limb
  3. NCC inhibition in the distal convoluted tubule
  4. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism
  5. ENaC blockade in the collecting system
Answer and explanation

Carbonic anhydrase inhibition

Acetazolamide reduces bicarbonate reabsorption, predominantly in the proximal tubule.

Option explanations

Carbonic anhydrase inhibition: Acetazolamide reduces bicarbonate reabsorption, predominantly in the proximal tubule.

NKCC2 inhibition in the thick ascending limb: Loop diuretics inhibit sodium-potassium-chloride transport in the thick ascending limb. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

NCC inhibition in the distal convoluted tubule: Thiazides inhibit the distal sodium-chloride cotransporter. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism: Spironolactone and eplerenone block aldosterone signaling and reduce potassium secretion. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

ENaC blockade in the collecting system: Amiloride and triamterene directly block epithelial sodium channels. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
